source_lines.36: Consider a commutative diagram of module homomorphisms with exact rows:
source_lines.45: 1. If $a$ is surjective and $b,d$ are injective, then $c$ is injective.
source_lines.46: 2. If $b,d$ are surjective and $e$ is injective, then $c$ is surjective.
source_lines.70: 1.1 Assume $a$ is surjective and $b,d$ are injective, and let $z\in C$ satisfy $c(z)=0$. Then [C3] gives $d(w(z))=w'(c(z))=0$, so injectivity of $d$ gives $w(z)=0$. [assume-hyp, C3, F2]
source_lines.72: 1.2 Assume $b,d$ are surjective and $e$ is injective, and let $z'\in C'$. By surjectivity of $d$, choose $q\in D$ with $d(q)=w'(z')$. [assume-hyp, F2, choose]
source_lines.74: 2.1 Exactness gives $y\in B$ with $v(y)=z$. By [C2], $v'(b(y))=c(v(y))=0$, so exactness gives $y'\in A'$ with $u'(y')=b(y)$. [step 1.1, C2, F1, choose]
source_lines.76: 2.2 By [C4], $e(x(q))=x'(d(q))=x'w'(z')=0$; injectivity of $e$ gives $x(q)=0$. Exactness gives $z\in C$ with $w(z)=q$. [step 1.2, C4, F1, F2, choose]
source_lines.78: 3.1 Surjectivity of $a$ gives $y'=a(t)$ for some $t\in A$. Then [C1] gives $b(y-u(t))=0$; injectivity of $b$ gives $y=u(t)$, and exactness gives $z=v(y)=v(u(t))=0$. Thus $c$ is injective. [step 2.1, C1, F1, F2, choose]
source_lines.80: 3.2 Now $w'(c(z)-z')=d(w(z))-w'(z')=0$ by [C3], so exactness gives $y'\in B'$ with $v'(y')=c(z)-z'$. Surjectivity of $b$ gives $y'=b(y)$; then [C2] yields $c(z-v(y))=z'$. Thus $c$ is surjective. [step 1.2, step 2.2, C2, C3, F1, F2, choose]
